title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol close: faith antecedent to execution not to eternal will; Minor — temporal prereqs
pass_a_gloss: The consideration of Peter as faithful and purged from sins will now be antecedent to the execution of the thing willed; namely the acquisition of salvation, and that from the decree of God: but it will not be antecedent to the very will of God concerning saving Peter, who decreed both, both to save Peter, and before he is saved to gift him with faith. Nor does it weaken the immutability of the Divine nature that it is put that something is decreed as antecedent to the actual production of the thing decreed, which is not antecedent to the internal volition of God concerning the thing to be produced. The reason is plain; Because the Effect of salvation in the predestinated subject and the decree of salvation to be given in the will of the predestinating One are diverse things, and do not require the same causes or previous conditions. Concerning the Minor I say nothing else, than that many things are prerequired in order that someone be saved in time, which were not prerequired in order that he be elected from eternity to salvation, but rather means afterward to be conferred on the predestinated in order that he be led through to salvation.
pass_b_english: Peter as faithful and purged of sins is antecedent to executing what was willed — acquiring salvation, by God's decree — but not antecedent to God's will to save Peter, who decreed both: to save Peter, and to gift him faith before he is saved. Nor does that unsettle divine immutability: something may be decreed as antecedent to actually producing what was decreed without being antecedent to God's internal volition about producing it. Reason: the effect of salvation in the predestinated subject and the decree to give salvation in the predestinating will are diverse things and do not require the same prior causes or conditions. On the Minor: many things are prerequired for someone to be saved in time that were not prerequired for eternal election to salvation — rather means later conferred on the predestinated so he is led through to salvation.
source_text: Erit jam consideratio Petri ut fidelis et a peccatis purgati antecedanea ad exsecutionem rei volitae; salutis scilicet acquisitionem, idque ex decreto Dei: sed non erit antecedanea ad ipsam voluntatem Dei de Petro servando, qui utrumque decrevit, et servare Petrum, et priusquam servetur fide illum donare. Neque immutabilitatem Divinae naturae labefactat quod ponitur, decernere aliquid tanquam praecedaneum ad rei decretae actualem productionem, quod non est praecedaneum ad internam Dei de re producenda volitionem. Ratio manifesta est; Quia Effectum salutis in subjecto praedestinato et decretum salutis dandae in voluntate praedestinantis sunt res diversae, nec easdem causas aut conditiones previas requirunt. De Minore nil aliud dico, quam multa praerequiri ut quis in tempore salvatur, quae non erant praerequisita ut ab aeterno ad salutem eligeretur, sed potius media praedestinato postmodum conferenda ut ad salutem perduceretur.
